HuangEtAl_2025.full_citation: Huang, et al. (2025). Artificial social intelligence in teamwork. European Journal of Education.
HuangEtAl_2025.tldr: Experiment in which three-person teams exchange real-time text-based advice with an AI advisor. Evaluates how AI affects teamwork processes through bidirectional communication (a flexible prompt–response system).
HuangEtAl_2025.actionable_insight: Used for designing AI intervention timing and method.

SchmutzEtAl_2024.full_citation: Schmutz, Outland, Kerstan, Georganta, Ulfert (2024). AI-Teaming: Redefining Collaboration in the Digital Era. Administrative Sciences.
SchmutzEtAl_2024.tldr: Recent review summarizing the current research landscape on trust, team dynamics, and shared cognition in Human–AI Teams (HATs).
SchmutzEtAl_2024.actionable_insight: As the most recent comprehensive HAIT review, essential for summarizing the current research landscape in the Literature Review section.

ThalerEtAl_2010.full_citation: Thaler, Sunstein, Balz (2010). Choice Architecture. Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences.
ThalerEtAl_2010.tldr: Overall, choice architecture interventions overall promote behavior change with a small to medium effect size of Cohen’s d = 0.45, and interventions that target the organization and structure of choice alternatives (decision structure) consistently outperform interventions that focus on the description of alternatives or the reinforcement of behavioral intentions (Decision assistance).
ThalerEtAl_2010.actionable_insight: Theoretical foundation for framing the AI as a choice architect. Mapping ACI's facilitative questioning onto one of these six tools strengthens the operational definition of ACI.

Weidmann_2025.full_citation: Weidmann, B. (2025). Measuring Human Leadership Skills with AI Agents. Sustainability.
Weidmann_2025.tldr: To fully leverage human–Gen AI collaboration, financial services firms should upskill employees, strengthen data reliability through robust governance, establish trusted AI systems, and effectively integrate Gen AI into workflows through strong managerial oversight.
Weidmann_2025.actionable_insight: Empirical justification for treating AI as a social agent (peer or leader). Direct empirical precedent for the AI Status variable.

StasserTitus_1985.full_citation: Stasser, G., Titus, W. (1985). Pooling of Unshared Information in Group Decision Making: Biased Information Sampling During Discussion. Journal of Experimental Social Psychology.
StasserTitus_1985.tldr: Foundational study demonstrating that groups often fail to reach optimal decisions because members hide unshared information they uniquely possess while repeatedly discussing shared information — a pattern called biased information sampling.
StasserTitus_1985.actionable_insight: Origin of the Hidden Profile paradigm and the foundational problem statement for why groups bury unshared information.

SeeberEtAl_2020.full_citation: Seeber, I., et al. (2020). Machines as teammates: A research agenda on AI in team collaboration. International Journal of Manpower.
SeeberEtAl_2020.tldr: The authors found that organisational support mechanisms such as facilitating environment, training opportunities and ensuring a viable technological competence level before organising human workers in teams with robots are important.
SeeberEtAl_2020.actionable_insight: Essential theory for establishing the AI Status (Leader vs. Peer) variable. Used when arguing why it is important to grant AI a status rather than treat it as a simple aide.

ChenEtAl_2025.full_citation: Chen, X., et al. (2025). Maintaining Balanced Conflict: Proactive Intervention Strategies of AI Voice Agents in Online Collaboration of Temporary Design Teams. Frontiers in Human Dynamics.
ChenEtAl_2025.tldr: A novel perspective on human-computer interaction is presented, framing it as a dynamic interplay between human and computational agents within a networked system, and a framework for communication spaces is introduced that systematically accommodate both autonomy-preserving and integration-seeking configurations within a shared formal foundation.
ChenEtAl_2025.actionable_insight: Excellent reference for describing the specific intervention behaviors by which a Leader-status AI guides team discussion and elicits unshared information.

ZercherEtAl_2025.full_citation: Zercher, D., et al. (2025). How Can Teams Benefit From AI Team Members? Exploring the Effect of Generative AI on Decision-Making Processes and Decision Quality in Team–AI Collaboration. Journal of Organizational Behavior.
ZercherEtAl_2025.tldr: Team–AI collaboration depends on effective teamwork between human and AI members, and teams with centralized AI knowledge make more accurate decisions than human teams due to reduced decision‐making asymmetries, trust in AI, beneficial AI information processing, and a balanced AI collaboration focus.
ZercherEtAl_2025.actionable_insight: Analyzes the effect of AI role on team performance and AI knowledge configuration. Demonstrates that without social validation information cannot be integrated even when present. The Common Prompt in common_framework.yaml is adapted from this work.

Miller_2019.full_citation: Miller, T. (2019). Explanation in artificial intelligence: Insights from the social sciences. Information Fusion.
Miller_2019.tldr: Previous efforts to define explainability in Machine Learning are summarized, establishing a novel definition that covers prior conceptual propositions with a major focus on the audience for which explainability is sought, and a taxonomy of recent contributions related to the explainability of different Machine Learning models are proposed.
Miller_2019.actionable_insight: Provides the operational definition of explanation and the standard XAI benchmark for comparing how ACI differs.

MillerIII_1977.full_citation: Miller III (1977). Review of Status Characteristics Theory (title not specified in source list). Implementation Science.
MillerIII_1977.tldr: The CFIR provides a pragmatic structure for approaching complex, interacting, multi-level, and transient states of constructs in the real world by embracing, consolidating, and unifying key constructs from published implementation theories.
MillerIII_1977.actionable_insight: Useful for grasping the development of SCT underlying the AI Status variable.

BergerEtAl_1972.full_citation: Berger, J., Cohen, B. P., Zelditch, M. (1972). Status Characteristics and Social Interaction. Acta Sociologica.
BergerEtAl_1972.tldr: Foundational classic sociology paper that first established the framework of Status Characteristics Theory.
BergerEtAl_1972.actionable_insight: Grounds the use of SCT indicators in designing the Leader condition — the justification for how human participants are made to perceive the AI as a Leader.

BrodbeckEtAl_2007.full_citation: Brodbeck, F. C., Kerschreiter, R., Mojzisch, A., Schulz-Hardt, S. (2007). Group Decision Making Under Conditions of Distributed Knowledge: The Information Asymmetries Model. Journal of Management.
BrodbeckEtAl_2007.tldr: Major paper that applies Status Characteristics Theory to explain why information is not adequately shared in group decision-making.
BrodbeckEtAl_2007.actionable_insight: Root of Zercher's Information Asymmetries Model (IAM). Strong theoretical basis for combining Leader × ACI in this study.

GanapiniEtAl_2023.full_citation: Ganapini, M. B., Campbell, M., Ho, K. (2023). Value-based Fast and Slow AI Nudging.
GanapiniEtAl_2023.tldr: Proposes an alternative, value-based conceptual framework for AI nudging that guides human behavior.
GanapiniEtAl_2023.actionable_insight: Smoothly connects ACI with nudge theory. Directly usable for the nudge scope principles and guidelines of ACI.

LuEtAl_2012.full_citation: Lu, L., Yuan, Y. C., McLeod, P. L. (2012). Twenty-Five Years of Hidden Profiles in Group Decision Making: A Meta-Analysis. Tourism Management.
LuEtAl_2012.tldr: Meta-analysis statistically synthesizing effect sizes and conditions across 25 years of Hidden Profile research.
LuEtAl_2012.actionable_insight: Reference for core experimental design parameters (information distribution ratios, group-size effect sizes, condition specifications).

ChiangEtAl_2024.full_citation: C. Chiang, Zhuoran Lu, Zhuoyan Li, Ming Yin (2024). Enhancing AI-Assisted Group Decision Making through LLM-Powered Devil's Advocate.
ChiangEtAl_2024.tldr: Through a randomized human-subject experiment, evidence is found suggesting that LLM-powered devil’s advocates that argue against the AI model’s decision recommendation have the potential to promote groups’ appropriate reliance on AI.
ChiangEtAl_2024.actionable_insight: Deploy LLM-powered contrastive arguments that directly challenge the AI recommendation (not group consensus) to calibrate appropriate reliance on AI in group decisions; interactive framing increases perceived collaboration.

JohnsonEtAl_2026.full_citation: Janet G. Johnson, Renkun Huang, Khoa Quoc Nguyen, Ji Young Nam, Michael Nebeling (2026). “I Felt Bad After We Ignored Her”: Understanding How Interface-Driven Social Prominence Shapes Group Discussions with GenAI.
JohnsonEtAl_2026.tldr: This paper introduces interface-driven social prominence as a design lens for collaborative GenAI systems and presents a GenAI-based conversational agent that can actively engage in spoken dialogue during video calls and designs three distinct collaboration modes that vary the social prominence of the agent by manipulating its presence in the shared space and the degree of control users have over it.
JohnsonEtAl_2026.actionable_insight: Vary GenAI agent's visual/spatial prominence and control allocation in shared interface to modulate its perceived status and influence on group discussion dynamics.
